FILED by the reviewing session (2026-11-28) with #5560 / #5561, from the audit table of docs/not-supported.md ns-regex-escapes (escapes that silently never match).

THE SHAPE (probe, perl 5.40.3 vs main cababb9d):
    print (("aa" =~ /(a)\g{-1}/ ? "m" : "n"), " ", ("abab" =~ /(a)(b)\g{-2}\g{-1}/ ? "m" : "n"), "\n");   # perl m m    PCL n n

SEMANTICS: `\g{-N}` is the N-th group OPENED before this point, counted backwards; `\g{N}` / `\gN` are absolute (measure: right today?), `\g{name}` = `\k<name>`.  The rewriter knows the count of groups opened so far, so the translation to an absolute `\N` is static.

RARE, so by the ruling of 2026-11-24 it is taken only where it falls out of the same arm as an ordinary member (#5560 / #5561 edit the same dispatch).

=== DONE (s543u) ===
Taken in the same arm (frequency rare): \gN \g{N} -> (?:\N), \g-N \g{-N} counted back from the capturing groups the rewrite scan has opened (a new NCAP counter), \g{name} -> \k<name>; \g0 and a reference before the first group die with perl's words.  The absolute spellings never matched either (cl-ppcre read the letter g).  p3c-g rows 1-6 perl = tree.  Guard row 78.
